whatis.intro: A reorder point is the stock level on a line that says the next order has to go in now. It holds enough stock to cover sales until the truck unloads, plus a buffer for surprises. With this calculator's defaults, that level is 709 cases.

cards.title: Supplier wait time, stated in cases
cards.body: Time, priced in cases. It takes the days you wait on a supplier and states them as a stock level you can check on the floor.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the wait on a supplier priced in cases

cards.title: It misses cases already on order
cards.body: Cases already on the way. The basic sum checks the floor only, so hold the trigger against stock on hand plus stock on order, or you order twice.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for stock already on order

cards.title: When accounts order on one day
cards.body: A day of usage is an average. When most accounts order for Monday's trucks, 141 cases of headroom can go in a single morning.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for headroom that goes in one busy morning

who.h2: Who uses a reorder point calculator
who.intro: Buyers at distributors that hold stock in their own warehouse use it to decide when each line needs a supplier order. Whoever places supplier orders should run it for each line, not once for the whole range.

look.h2: Three checks before you trust a reorder point
look.intro: The sum is simple. The trouble is in the stock and the buffer you feed it, and in the units you count them in.

steps.title: On hand means free to sell
steps.body: Take out cases already picked or promised to orders that are in. 850 cases on the floor is less than 850 free if tomorrow's orders already claim part of it.

steps.title: A buffer sized for this supplier
steps.body: The 229 cases you type in were sized for one lead time. Change the supplier or the lead time and size the buffer again before you trust the trigger.

steps.title: One unit in every field
steps.body: Usage, buffer and the count all have to be in full cases. A count taken in eaches or broken cases makes the days left read wrong.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits around your trigger
vos.h3: Customer orders draw each line toward its trigger
vos.body: VOS does not set your reorder point, count your stock or order from your suppliers. It works on the demand side, where inventory visibility follows order activity as customers order by voice in the VOS app.
